name: Neural_Signaling
description: Electrochemical mechanisms by which neurons generate and transmit electrical signals along axons and across synapses.

name: Sensory_Systems
description: Neural pathways and cortical circuits that transform peripheral sensory signals into structured internal representations.

name: Motor_Systems
description: Cortical, subcortical, and spinal circuits that plan, initiate, and execute voluntary and reflexive movement.

name: Synaptic_Plasticity
description: Activity-dependent mechanisms by which synaptic strength and neural circuit connectivity are modified in response to experience.

name: Neural_Circuits_and_Oscillations
description: The organisation of neurons into functional networks and the rhythmic population-level dynamics that coordinate information processing.

name: Neurochemistry
description: Molecular mechanisms of neurotransmitter synthesis, release, receptor binding, and neuromodulatory signalling that govern neural function.

name: Electrical_Signaling
description: The biophysical basis of neuronal excitability, including resting membrane potential, action potential generation, and signal propagation.

name: Synaptic_Transmission
description: The sequence of events at the synapse from presynaptic action potential to postsynaptic receptor activation and signal termination.

name: Neural_Integration
description: The spatial and temporal summation of synaptic inputs at the dendrite and soma that determines whether a neuron reaches firing threshold.

name: Visual_Processing
description: The transformation of photoreceptor activation into increasingly complex cortical representations of luminance, orientation, motion, and object identity.

name: Auditory_Processing
description: The encoding of sound frequency, intensity, and timing from cochlear hair cells through brainstem nuclei to auditory cortex.

name: Somatosensory_Processing
description: The encoding and central representation of touch, pressure, proprioception, and pain from peripheral receptors to somatosensory cortex.

name: Cortical_Motor_Control
description: The role of motor and premotor cortex in encoding movement parameters and transmitting commands via descending pathways.

name: Subcortical_Motor_Circuits
description: Contributions of the basal ganglia, cerebellum, and thalamus to action selection, movement coordination, and error correction.

name: Activity_Dependent_Plasticity
description: Hebbian and anti-Hebbian forms of long-lasting synaptic change driven by correlated pre- and postsynaptic activity.

name: Homeostatic_Plasticity
description: Compensatory mechanisms that stabilise neuronal firing rates and maintain network dynamics within functional ranges.

name: Structural_Plasticity
description: Changes in the morphology of dendritic spines, axonal arbors, and synaptic contact sites as substrates for long-term circuit modification.

name: Network_Oscillations
description: Synchronised rhythmic activity across neural populations at characteristic frequencies, reflecting circuit dynamics and coordinating inter-area communication.

name: Cortical_Architecture
description: The laminar, columnar, and areal organisation of the neocortex and its implications for input-output routing and local circuit computation.

name: Inhibitory_Circuits
description: The morphologically and physiologically diverse GABAergic interneurons that shape network dynamics through feedforward and feedback inhibition.

name: Excitatory_Neurotransmission
description: Glutamate-mediated fast excitatory signalling through ionotropic receptors and its role in synaptic strength and plasticity.

name: Inhibitory_Neurotransmission
description: GABA-mediated inhibitory signalling through ionotropic and metabotropic receptors and its role in network stabilisation and oscillations.

name: Neuromodulatory_Systems
description: Diffuse ascending projections using dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, and norepinephrine that regulate neural gain and circuit state.

name: Voltage_Gated_Channel_Kinetics
description: The voltage-dependent opening and closing dynamics of sodium, potassium, and calcium channels that underlie action potential generation and repolarisation.

name: Action_Potential_Propagation
description: The active spread of an action potential along the axon, maintained by successive activation of voltage-gated sodium channels ahead of the impulse.

name: Saltatory_Conduction
description: The rapid propagation of action potentials in myelinated axons through discrete jumps between nodes of Ranvier, dramatically increasing conduction velocity.

name: Vesicle_Release_Mechanisms
description: Calcium-triggered SNARE-mediated fusion of synaptic vesicles with the presynaptic membrane, releasing neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft.

name: Postsynaptic_Receptor_Activation
description: The binding of released neurotransmitter to ionotropic and metabotropic receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, producing changes in conductance and second-messenger signalling.

name: Neurotransmitter_Reuptake
description: The clearance of released neurotransmitter from the synaptic cleft through transporter-mediated reuptake into presynaptic terminals and surrounding glia.

name: Temporal_Summation
description: The integration of successive subthreshold postsynaptic potentials within a short time window, enabling suprathreshold excitation from high-frequency presynaptic input.

name: Spatial_Summation
description: The simultaneous integration of inputs from multiple synaptic locations along the dendritic tree, enabling suprathreshold excitation from spatially distributed input.

name: Dendritic_Computation
description: Active conductances in dendrites that enable nonlinear integration, local processing, and coincidence detection independent of the soma.

name: Retinal_Encoding
description: The transformation of photoreceptor signals by retinal interneurons into ganglion cell spike trains, generating centre-surround receptive fields sensitive to contrast.

name: Orientation_Selectivity
description: The tuning of primary visual cortex neurons to the angle of elongated stimuli, arising from the arrangement of thalamic inputs and local cortical circuits.

name: Ventral_Stream_Processing
description: The hierarchical transformation of visual representations along the occipito-temporal pathway from simple features in V1 to complex object representations in IT cortex.

name: Cochlear_Transduction
description: The mechanoelectrical conversion of sound-induced basilar membrane displacement into hair cell receptor potentials and auditory nerve firing.

name: Tonotopic_Organisation
description: The spatial mapping of sound frequency along the basilar membrane and preserved at successive levels of the auditory pathway including primary auditory cortex.

name: Sound_Localisation
description: The computation of sound source azimuth and elevation from interaural time and level differences by brainstem nuclei including the medial superior olive.

name: Mechanoreceptor_Subtypes
description: The four classes of low-threshold mechanoreceptors in glabrous skin — Meissner, Merkel, Ruffini, and Pacinian corpuscles — each tuned to distinct tactile features.

name: Somatosensory_Cortex_Organisation
description: The somatotopic map of body surface in primary somatosensory cortex, with representational area scaling with receptor density rather than body-surface area.

name: Nociception
description: The transduction of noxious thermal, mechanical, and chemical stimuli by nociceptors and their transmission via Aδ and C fibres to the dorsal horn and brain.

name: Motor_Cortex_Topography
description: The somatotopic organisation of primary motor cortex encoding of voluntary movement, with representation area scaling with movement precision rather than muscle mass.

name: Corticospinal_Tract
description: The direct descending projection from motor cortex to spinal motor neurons, enabling fine voluntary control of distal limb musculature.

name: Population_Vector_Coding
description: The representation of intended movement direction by the weighted sum of preferred-direction vectors across a population of motor cortex neurons.

name: Basal_Ganglia_Action_Selection
description: The role of direct and indirect striato-pallidal pathways in selecting motor programmes and suppressing competing actions through inhibitory gating of thalamus.

name: Cerebellar_Error_Correction
description: The use of climbing fibre-encoded error signals to adjust Purkinje cell responses, enabling the cerebellum to refine motor timing and correct movement errors.

name: Thalamocortical_Motor_Loops
description: The reciprocal connections between motor thalamic nuclei and cortex that relay basal ganglia and cerebellar output to motor and premotor cortex.

name: Long_Term_Potentiation
description: The persistent strengthening of a synapse following high-frequency stimulation or correlated pre- and postsynaptic activity, dependent on NMDA receptor activation.

name: Long_Term_Depression
description: The persistent weakening of a synapse following low-frequency stimulation or temporally uncorrelated activity, often mediated by mGluR or NMDA receptor activation.

name: Spike_Timing_Dependent_Plasticity
description: The asymmetric plasticity rule in which synapses strengthen when the presynaptic spike precedes postsynaptic firing and weaken when the order is reversed.

name: Synaptic_Scaling
description: The global multiplicative adjustment of all synaptic strengths in a neuron in response to prolonged changes in activity, maintaining firing rates within a functional range.

name: Intrinsic_Excitability_Regulation
description: Homeostatic changes in voltage-gated channel expression and membrane conductance that adjust a neuron's input-output gain following sustained perturbations in activity.

name: Dendritic_Spine_Remodeling
description: Activity-dependent changes in the size, shape, and number of dendritic spines that alter synaptic strength and provide a structural correlate of plasticity.

name: Axonal_Sprouting_and_Pruning
description: The growth of new axonal branches and elimination of redundant projections during development and in response to learning, reshaping circuit connectivity.

name: Gamma_Oscillations
description: Synchronised oscillations in the 30–80 Hz range arising from interneuron-pyramidal cell interactions, implicated in local computation and inter-area binding.

name: Theta_Rhythms
description: Oscillations in the 4–12 Hz range prominent in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex during active exploration, organising sequential neural activity and spatial coding.

name: Sleep_Oscillations
description: The stereotyped sequence of slow oscillations, sleep spindles, and sharp-wave ripples during non-REM sleep, supporting memory consolidation through hippocampal-cortical dialogue.

name: Cortical_Lamination
description: The organisation of neocortex into six layers with distinct cell types, connectivity profiles, and input-output relationships defining canonical cortical circuits.

name: Topographic_Mapping
description: The systematic spatial correspondence between the arrangement of neurons in cortical areas and the spatial or feature organisation of their inputs.

name: Cortical_Columns
description: Vertical modules of neurons sharing similar response properties, arising from common thalamic input and local intracortical circuitry, observed across sensory and motor areas.

name: GABAergic_Interneuron_Diversity
description: The multiple morphological and electrophysiological classes of cortical inhibitory interneurons — including parvalbumin, somatostatin, and VIP subtypes — with distinct circuit roles.

name: Feedforward_Inhibition
description: Inhibitory postsynaptic potentials evoked by the same afferent pathway that drives excitation, restricting the temporal window for integration and limiting polysynaptic spread.

name: Feedback_Inhibition
description: Inhibition driven by the output of a local excitatory neuron onto itself or its neighbours via interneurons, implementing gain control and preventing runaway excitation.

name: AMPA_Receptor_Dynamics
description: The rapid kinetics and regulated surface trafficking of AMPA receptors at the postsynaptic density, which determine the amplitude and expression of synaptic plasticity.

name: NMDA_Receptor_Function
description: The voltage- and ligand-gated properties of NMDA receptors that detect coincident pre- and postsynaptic activity, serving as a molecular coincidence detector for plasticity induction.

name: GABA_Receptor_Subtypes
description: The pharmacological and biophysical diversity of GABA-A and GABA-B receptors, determining the kinetics and spatial spread of inhibitory postsynaptic currents.

name: Chloride_Homeostasis
description: The regulation of intracellular chloride concentration by KCC2 and NKCC1 co-transporters, which sets the reversal potential of GABA-A mediated currents and determines whether GABA is inhibitory or excitatory.

name: Dopaminergic_Pathways
description: The mesolimbic, mesocortical, and nigrostriatal dopaminergic projections from ventral tegmental area and substantia nigra, modulating striatal and prefrontal circuit function.

name: Serotonergic_Circuits
description: Projections from raphe nuclei to virtually all brain regions, modulating arousal, mood, and sensory gain through G-protein-coupled serotonin receptors.

name: Cholinergic_Modulation
description: Basal forebrain and brainstem cholinergic projections that enhance cortical signal-to-noise ratio and regulate arousal state through muscarinic and nicotinic receptor activation.

name: Synaptic_Strength
description: The amplitude of the postsynaptic potential produced by a single presynaptic action potential, determined by vesicle release probability and receptor number and conductance.

name: Conduction_Velocity
description: The speed at which action potentials propagate along an axon, determined by axon diameter and degree of myelination.

name: Excitation_Inhibition_Balance
description: The ratio of excitatory to inhibitory synaptic drive impinging on a neuron or local network, which sets the operating point for information processing and neural gain.

name: Receptor_Sensitivity
description: The magnitude of postsynaptic current per unit of neurotransmitter concentration, determined by receptor density, subunit composition, and state-dependent modulation.

name: Neural_Gain
description: The steepness of the input-output transfer function relating injected current to firing rate, which determines how sharply a neuron responds to changes in input strength.

name: Oscillation_Frequency
description: The dominant frequency of synchronised neural population activity in a given circuit, shaped by interneuron time constants and conduction delays.

name: Myelination_Density
description: The degree of axonal myelination across a fibre tract, which determines conduction velocity and metabolic efficiency of long-range signalling.

name: Plasticity_Threshold
description: The minimum level of correlated synaptic co-activation required to trigger long-term potentiation, set by postsynaptic calcium dynamics and kinase activity.

name: Release_Probability
description: The probability that a presynaptic action potential triggers vesicle fusion at a given synapse, a major determinant of short-term synaptic dynamics.

name: Spontaneous_Firing_Rate
description: The baseline discharge rate of a neuron in the absence of specific input, reflecting tonic excitatory drive and intrinsic membrane properties.

name: Hodgkin_Huxley_Model
description: A conductance-based mathematical model describing action potential generation in terms of voltage-dependent sodium and potassium channel kinetics, derived from squid giant axon recordings.

name: Hebbian_Learning_Rule
description: The principle that synaptic strength increases when a presynaptic neuron persistently and repeatedly contributes to the firing of a postsynaptic neuron, providing a cellular basis for associative learning.

name: Rate_Coding
description: The hypothesis that neurons encode information primarily in their mean firing rate, with stimulus identity or intensity represented by the average number of spikes per unit time.

name: Temporal_Coding
description: The hypothesis that information is encoded in the precise timing of individual spikes or patterns of spike timing relative to a reference signal such as an oscillation.

name: Binding_by_Synchrony
description: The proposal that features of a perceptual object encoded in spatially distributed neurons are bound into a unified representation through synchronised gamma-band oscillations.

name: Critical_Period_Theory
description: The framework describing developmental windows of heightened synaptic plasticity during which sensory experience shapes cortical circuits, after which modification requires greater perturbation.

name: Population_Vector_Theory
description: The theory that motor cortex encodes intended movement direction as the vector sum of preferred-direction vectors weighted by the firing rate of each participating neuron.

name: Lateral_Inhibition
description: The principle that activation of a neuron suppresses its neighbours via inhibitory interneurons, sharpening spatial tuning, enhancing contrast, and preventing activity spread.

name: Three_Factor_Learning_Rule
description: An extension of Hebbian plasticity in which synaptic modification requires a third neuromodulatory signal — such as dopamine or acetylcholine — in addition to correlated pre- and postsynaptic activity.

name: Predictive_Coding
description: The theory that the brain generates hierarchical predictions about sensory input and transmits only precision-weighted prediction errors upward, minimising redundant signalling.

name: Cortical_Remyelination
description: The restoration of myelin sheaths to previously demyelinated axons through the differentiation and maturation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells.

name: Firing_Rate_Variability
description: The trial-to-trial variability in neuronal spike count for repeated identical stimuli, reflecting intrinsic stochasticity and network-level fluctuations.
